prompt: What does the Apple Developer Program cost a year, in US dollars, according to Apple's programs page on 30 October 2026?
With a free Personal Team, how long does an app installed from Xcode on your own iPhone keep working?

choices.text: Until the next iOS update
choices.why: The limit is the profile's, not the system's.

choices.text: Seven days, then you rebuild and reinstall
choices.why: Right, in Apple's words: profiles expire 7 days from issuance.

choices.text: A year, the same as a paid membership would give
choices.why: A year is the membership's renewal, not a free profile's life.

choices.text: It cannot be installed on a phone at all without paying
choices.why: A free account does install on your own device, with limits.

prompt: A student wants to publish their own free app. Can they ask for the fee waiver?
hint: Read who the waiver page excludes.

choices.text: Yes, since the app is free
choices.why: Being free is required, but the waiver is for organisations.

choices.text: Yes, if they show a student card
choices.why: The page names accredited institutions, not their students.

choices.text: No: individuals are not eligible
choices.why: Right: the page excludes individuals and single-person businesses.

choices.text: No, because free apps need no membership
choices.why: Any app on the App Store needs a membership.

prompt: A membership expires and is not renewed. What happens to the planner on phones that already have it?

choices.text: It keeps working, but is no longer offered for download
choices.why: Right, as Apple's renewal page says.

choices.text: It stops opening the day the membership ends
choices.why: Installed copies keep working, according to the page.

choices.text: It is deleted from every phone that has it within 24 hours
choices.why: Nothing is removed from phones.

choices.text: It keeps working and stays on the store for a year
choices.why: It leaves the store at expiry.

prompt: Which question does the provisioning profile answer?

choices.text: Who signed this?
choices.why: That is the certificate.

choices.text: Is this app, signed by them, allowed here and to do this?
choices.why: Right: App ID, certificates, devices and entitlements.

choices.text: What does the app want to do, and with which services?
choices.why: That is the entitlements.

choices.text: Has the app passed App Review?
choices.why: Review is lesson 22 and not part of signing.

prompt: Somebody changes one image inside a signed app and copies it to an iPhone. What does iOS do?

choices.text: Runs it, since images are not code
choices.why: The signature covers every file, not only code.

choices.text: Asks the person whether to trust it
choices.why: There is no such prompt for a broken signature.

choices.text: Refuses to launch it
choices.why: Right: the signature no longer matches the files.

choices.text: Re-signs it with the developer's key
choices.why: The device never holds the developer's private key.

prompt: A Mac has your Apple Development certificate and its private key, and Xcode says the certificate is not trusted. What is the likely missing piece?

choices.text: Apple's root certificate
choices.why: The root is built into every Apple device.

choices.text: The WWDR intermediate
choices.why: Right: without it the chain cannot reach the root.

choices.text: A provisioning profile for the device
choices.why: A profile is checked at install; trust is the chain's.

choices.text: A second private key
choices.why: One key per certificate; the key is there.

prompt: Who does an Apple Distribution certificate belong to?

choices.text: The developer who made it
choices.why: That is a development certificate.

choices.text: The team
choices.why: Right, one of each type per team, made by the Account Holder or an Admin.

choices.text: Apple, which lends it for each upload
choices.why: Apple issues it; the team owns and holds its key.

choices.text: The Mac it was made on
choices.why: The computer's name is appended to development certificates, not distribution ones.

prompt: Match each link of the chain to what it is.

pairs.right: Signed by the root, signs yours
Your public key and your name
Stays on your Mac and signs the app

right_distractors: Uploaded to Apple inside the request

prompt: What goes to Apple in a certificate signing request?
hint: Only one half of the key.

choices.text: The private key, so Apple can sign with it
choices.why: The private key never leaves your Mac.

choices.text: The public key and a name, signed with your private key
choices.why: Right: the signature proves you hold the private key.

choices.text: Both keys, encrypted with your Apple Account password
choices.why: Nothing private is sent, encrypted or not.

choices.text: The app itself, for Apple to sign
choices.why: You sign the app; the CSR is about your key.

prompt: `openssl req -verify` printed `Certificate request self-___ verify OK`, the proof that the sender holds the private key.
hint: One word, what the request carries of itself.

prompt: `ls -l` showed `dev.key` as `-rw-------` and the request as `-rw-r--r--`. Why the difference?

choices.text: `openssl` gets file permissions wrong for every key it writes
choices.why: It is deliberate.

choices.text: The request is larger, so it is shared
choices.why: Size has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: The key is the secret; the request is public
choices.why: Right: only you may read the key.

choices.text: The key was made first
choices.why: Order does not set permissions.

prompt: `openssl verify -CAfile root.pem dev.pem` failed with `unable to get local issuer certificate`. What would fix it, and what is the Mac equivalent?
hint: The first verify had one more argument.

choices.text: A new root, and on a Mac reinstalling Xcode
choices.why: The root was fine; a link was missing.

choices.text: Passing the intermediate; on a Mac, installing the current WWDR
choices.why: Right: with `-untrusted inter.pem` the chain closes.

choices.text: A new private key, and on a Mac revoking the certificate
choices.why: The key was never the problem.

choices.text: Nothing: the certificate is forged
choices.why: The same file verified once the intermediate was given.

prompt: Put section 05's toy chain in the order it was built.
hint: Your key first, the verdict last.

prompt: Which profile names no devices?

choices.text: iOS App Development
choices.why: It lists your registered devices.

choices.text: Ad Hoc
choices.why: It lists the testers' registered devices.

choices.text: App Store Connect
choices.why: Right: the store installs on every device after review.

choices.text: None: every profile lists devices
choices.why: The App Store one does not.

prompt: A build that installed yesterday will not install today, and nothing in the code changed. What is the first thing to check?

choices.text: The profile's expiry date
choices.why: Right: `security cms -D -i` shows its `ExpirationDate`.

choices.text: The Swift version of the toolchain
choices.why: Nothing was rebuilt with a new compiler.

choices.text: The App Review status of the app
choices.why: Installing from Xcode involves no review.

choices.text: Whether the bundle identifier is still free
choices.why: It was yours yesterday and still is.

prompt: Why can an app not grant itself push notifications by adding a key to `Info.plist` after it is signed?
hint: Where does iOS read entitlements from?

choices.text: `Info.plist` is read-only once an app is on an iPhone
choices.why: It is inside the signed bundle like everything else; that is not the reason.

choices.text: Entitlements are read from the signature
choices.why: Right, and the profile has to allow them.

choices.text: Push needs a usage string in `Info.plist` first
choices.why: Notifications ask with their own call, not a usage string.

choices.text: Only Apple may edit an app's files
choices.why: Anybody can edit; the signature then breaks.

prompt: The app's entitlements say `aps-environment` is `production`; the profile says `development`. What does `check-entitlements.swift` print, and what is the fix?

choices.text: `ok`, because both have the key
choices.why: The values have to match too.

choices.text: `refused`, and the fix is editing the profile
choices.why: A profile is signed by Apple; editing it breaks it.

choices.text: `refused`, with both values; sign with a matching profile
choices.why: Right: a distribution profile says production.

choices.text: Nothing: the checker ignores push
choices.why: It checks every claimed key.

prompt: Run on `More.entitlements`, with HealthKit added, what exit status did `check-entitlements.swift` give?
When does a team turn automatic signing off?
hint: When Xcode on one Mac is not the one deciding.

choices.text: Always, since manual signing is more secure than automatic signing
choices.why: It is more explicit, not more secure.

choices.text: For a build server, or a shared distribution identity
choices.why: Right: those need a written-down choice.

choices.text: When the app has no capabilities
choices.why: That is the easiest case for automatic signing.

choices.text: Once a free account becomes a paid one
choices.why: Automatic signing works with both.

prompt: Why keep an archive after it has been uploaded?

choices.text: App Store Connect deletes builds after a week
choices.why: That is not the reason given.

choices.text: A new version must be built from the old archive
choices.why: A new version is a new build.

choices.text: Its dSYM turns crash addresses into function names
choices.why: Right: without it that build's crashes cannot be read.

choices.text: It holds the private key needed for the next upload to the store
choices.why: The key lives in the keychain, not in archives.

prompt: Which destination does Archive need in Xcode?
hint: The simulator is not a device.

choices.text: The simulator you last ran
choices.why: An archive is built for devices.

choices.text: Any iOS Device
choices.why: Right, `generic/platform=iOS` at the command line.

choices.text: My Mac, with Mac Catalyst
choices.why: That builds a Mac app.

choices.text: Whatever the scheme's Run action uses
choices.why: Archive has its own destination and Release configuration.
